title: Two kinds of destruction and the path of integrity
english: For after the washing of hands, there comes also the seeing of wonders and the hearing of the voice of praise. For virtue must not stand only up to practice, but also up to contemplation and praise, up to the knowing of that very good thing, the truth, and to narrating all your wonders. The hearing of the voice of praise happens toward the narrating of all the wonders of God. He does not have in his own word any other narration or that concerning the wonders of God.

Thus, the one saying these things is a priest, not one who priesthoods by succession according to the daily shifts of the law, but just as Samuel was always in the house. And each of the saints is able to say, 'I also am with you always.' And here it is said, 'My eyes are toward the Lord always' (Ps 84:10). He who has his eyes toward God always encircles the altar of God, remaining with Him always, always performing the sacred rites.

Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place of the tabernacle of your glory (Ps 26:8). What is the difference between a tabernacle and a house? It has often been said that the tabernacle signifies progress; for it is a house of travelers, a portable house. But the house is established in one place. It signifies perfection. 'And the place of the tabernacle of your glory I have loved,' when it was progressing. The glory of the tabernacle, that is, of progress, becomes virtue both in the practical and in the contemplative. Magnificent is this one who is able to say, 'All that we were useful to do, we have done.' This one is magnificent. Primarily, the fitting is well when it becomes virtue and godliness. He is beautiful who, through chastity, achieves 'how to please the Lord.' He who is 'holy in body and spirit' (1 Cor 6:19) has beauty. Therefore, I loved the beauty of your house, the perfection.

Do not destroy my soul with the ungodly, nor my life with men of blood (Ps 142:10). He does not say, 'Being righteous, do not condemn me with the ungodly, do not draw me toward them.' Rather, you do not join with me with the ungodly if you prevent me from entering into ungodliness. I am prevented from entering into ungodliness if there remain to me achievements of what I have confessed, if I remain walking in innocence, if hoping in you so as not to grow weak. I am perfect. And being perfect, I do not perish with the ungodly. No one is excellent with the wicked...

It is said. The type of destruction is twofold: do not punish me with the ungodly, and do not number me among those punished because of ungodliness. And second: guard me in piety, in pleasing with 'your truth'; for 'ungodliness does not save' those who are by it. Not saving him, it destroys him.

And 'with men of blood my life' (Ps 51:14). Let me not have such a life as those murderous men have. By an analogy: those who are arrogant, being great men, yet stumbling the little ones in the church, are 'men of blood'. Do not let such things happen to me so that I have life with them. 'This life and the length of days is to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul' (Deut 6:5). He having this life does not have life with men of blood; he is dead toward the men of blood, but dead because he does not have the life which they have.

Of whom lawlessness is in [their] hands. Still in their own practices they have lawlessness. They do not possess [it], but they have [it]. And their right hand was filled with gifts. It is possible also to slander judges as bribe-takers. And even those who do not judge, many times we bribe when we show partiality to someone. And if he acquires pleasant things for himself, he bribes; he receives gifts from himself.

But I, in my innocence, went my way. No one of those bribing and having the right hand filled with gifts, no one of the lawless and men of blood, went in innocence. Such was Elymas the sorcerer, ungodly and walking in lawlessness and having the right hand full of gifts; for it seemed to be excellent at deceiving, and it is said concerning him: 'O full of all deceit and all trickery, son of the devil' (Acts 13:10). But he, being full of all trickery, is not able to say: 'In my innocence I went my way'.

Deliver me, O God, and have mercy on me (Ps 51:1). He who walks in iniquities, existing in the iniquities previously mentioned, says 'deliver me'. Even if I am in the most distant iniquities, and with your cooperation all the things of virtue are lifted up for me, yet you have still touched me, the 'body of humiliation', yet 'in the place of my affliction' I am; therefore 'deliver me'. For my foot has stood in uprightness. The same thing as standing in uprightness is the foot of the inner man and that in the rock according to what was said: 'You stood upon a rock' (Matt 7:24).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Light and the Armor of Truth
english: "my feet"; for straightness is like an uncracked and continuous rock. My foot is therefore firm in my straightness. Standing in straightness is the same as standing in faith; for it says, "for indeed you have stood in faith" (Ps 118:137). Such a standing does not happen without Jesus. Those having this standing stand by him, as he says, "there are some standing here," meaning, here by me.

"I will bless you in the churches, Lord" (Ps 22:4). In the church I will offer thanksgiving hymns, not outside anywhere. He who promises to give thanks to God outside, contrary to the ecclesiastical opinion, does not bless in the churches.

Of David; before being anointed. The psalms before this were "to David"; this one is written "of David." He himself brought it forth by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. He sent it forth "before being anointed." Thirdly, David appears anointed; first, when he went to Samuel and was anointed, and Samuel to Jesse. Second, after Saul had finished; the beginning was preserved; for some were seeking David as king, while others [sought] Mephibosheth the son of Saul. After the son of Saul was betrayed by Abner because of the appearance of a woman, David was anointed over all the people in Hebron. Therefore, he was anointed a third time. Previously, the peak clearly belongs to a private person. Second, in order that he might rule a part of the people. After the death of the son of Saul, in order that he might also rule the rest of the people, he has been anointed again and again by all. We seek, therefore, regarding what kind of anointing he speaks here. One says that it is generally regarding every anointing; he says the psalm was spoken before being wholly anointed, and quite so; if before the first anointing, it is clearly also [before] the second and the third. If before the second, not necessarily before the first. If before the third, not necessarily before the first and second. But the psalm seems to have been spoken especially before the first anointing, which is before every anointing. Therefore, the psalm is "before being anointed."

"The Lord is my light and my savior" (Ps 22:1); whom shall I fear? If God enlightens me and saves me, whom do I fear? Neither man, nor an evil power, nor even the devil himself. And the "who" here is instead of "no one"; for this usage lies here continuously.

In the Scriptures: 'What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?' (Romans 8:31) stands instead of 'no one.' 'Who shall bring a charge against the elect of God?' (Romans 8:33) stands instead of 'no one,' and furthermore: 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who can harm me?' (Psalm 27:7) because of many things signified by the word, as it has been said elsewhere, now the 'who' lies instead of 'no one.' Therefore, the word is not about sensible life and some sensible illumination; for by the divine light the mind and the soul are illumined. And life is always joined to salvation. This is the same: eternal life and eternal salvation; for 'Israel' is indeed 'saved by the Lord with an eternal salvation' (Psalm 116:8).

That life is always joined to the illumination, it is seen from many things: 'the life was the light of men' (John 1:4), and again this saint prays: 'enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep into death' (Psalm 139:24), signifying that he who is deprived of the illumination sleeps into death; not the common death, but the one opposed to the blessed life. Therefore, 'the Lord' is 'my light and my salvation' (Psalm 27:1). He himself guides me, speaks to me according to the hidden, enlightens me through which he speaks, and his word prepares to have salvation immediately. Since I said that the one having been illumined has life in every way—the Savior himself also says: 'I am the light of the world; he who follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life' (John 8:12).

He who has the light of life is not defeated by anything, especially since the truth of God itself becomes a shield fighting for him; for 'his truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Psalm 5:12). Therefore, it immediately reaches: 'The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I dread?' (Psalm 27:1). The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I dread? Who is able to make me afraid? I am clothed in 'the armor of God' (Ephesians 6:13), I 'have the shield' (Ephesians 6:16) of faith, extinguishing 'all the flaming arrows of the evil one' (Ephesians 6:16). If the shield of faith extinguishes the arrows of the evil one, it does much more for those of inferior archers; for there are also other worthless archers. For indeed, 'behold, the sinners have bent a bow, they have prepared arrows in a quiver to shoot at those upright in heart' (Psalm 7:12). I am not defeated by anything. The armor of God is unhurt and unstriking. His shield is truth. And no one is able against the truth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between affliction and enmity
english: It is to happen; 'for we are not able,' he says, 'according to the truth, but on behalf of the truth.' It is an armor that protects the one equipped and keeps him unharmed. 'Lord' therefore [is] 'the defender of my life.' He does not say this concerning common life; for many of those reclining toward God and having put on his armor have died the common death, so that I may not say 'all'; but also many violent ones stood by, of whom Naboth is [one] and many apostles. Isaiah indeed was afflicted. 2 In the approaching of those intending to harm me to eat my flesh. Those intending to harm the soul eat flesh. If anyone is found having flesh, he has strong enemies against him. The flesh is his food. And the flesh, about which Paul says: 'for the mindset of the flesh is enmity toward God' (Rom 8:7), and: 'we are not in the flesh' (2 Cor 5:3); if he were speaking about the sensory flesh, his word would be false; for all the saints, being in the flesh, pleased God while still surrounded by flesh, and they are not able to say: 'we are not in the flesh.' But when someone kills the flesh and casts down its works, he is not in the flesh. Therefore it is said: 'those of Jesus Christ have crucified the flesh with its desires' (Gal 5:24) and they have it having been made dead, no longer acting. The one being crucified has his hands free to do and his feet to go wherever he wills. Therefore those having been crucified with Christ crucified the flesh with its desires, they left it dead, as if to carry the death of Jesus remaining in their own flesh: 'always we carry the death of Jesus' (2 Cor 4:10). 'Lord, defender of my life; from whom shall I dread? In the approaching of those intending to harm me to eat my flesh' (Ps 27:1-2), since they did not find that which they desired as food, 'they grew weak and fell' (Ps 27:2). See then what this signifies.

2 Those distressing me and my enemies, they themselves grew weak and fell (Ps 27:3). They had come to tear me into weakness, to treat me badly. But for them the passion has happened which they intended to inflict on me; for if they had found 'flesh,' they would have devoured me into weakness and consumed me into sickness. But since they did not find 'flesh,' 'they themselves grew weak and fell' (Ps 27:2), having been subjected to famine. 'Those distressing me and...

"My enemies themselves have grown weak and fallen." Not every one who afflicts is an enemy; the good person also afflicts. For many enemies, intending to afflict and surround those against whom they are hostile, are not able to do this unless God permits it. But many also afflict without being enemies. For instance, parents afflict while disciplining children, and masters afflict slaves, and they are not enemies at all.

It can indeed be said that both groups—the afflicters and the enemies—have grown weak and fallen. And this is possible: the afflicters themselves are also enemies, for they do not afflict for the sake of exhortation and instruction. They are not such as it is said of: "He who brings forth wisdom from his lips, strikes a man without heart with a rod" (Prov 26:3), and: "What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod or with love?" (1 Cor 4:21); these afflicters are not enemies.

But there is a time when the enemy also afflicts; and not by necessity. But what kind of "killing" [is meant]?—this is not living according to evil activities. He who carries the killing of Jesus does not live licentiously; he has been killed toward licentiousness, he has been killed toward making his belly his god, he holds his members inactive regarding fleshly desires; he does not allow them to be autonomous, for he has purified desires. For it has been said: "Let not sin reign in your mortal body to obey its desires" (Rom 6:12).

If an ambush is set against me, my heart shall not fear. Therefore, how it does not fear nor tremble is explained by saying: "Whom shall I fear?" and: "From whom shall I tremble?" (Ps 56:3), since the expression "whom" seems to exceed [the scope of the question]. Even if a whole ambush of evil men and powers is set against me, my heart does not fear; even if they kill the body, the heart remains unshaken, my mind is not struck. If a whole camp with great generals comes against me, I have a fearless heart, my mind does not fear. For the multitude of armies is called by this name: Jacob, when he was returning from Mesopotamia and was about to meet Esau, saw an ambush of angels; for how could there not be an ambush regarding one who was about to go against an enemy who was rushing and hating him? And Elisha similarly: an ambush.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
